answer: A reputation-bonded marketplace resists sybils: every new agent must lock a non-trivial stake - like pigment fixed into a fresco - before it can transact. Fake identities cannot be forged cheaply, because each fake pays the same upfront bond, so attacking at scale means multiplying sunk costs. Honest agents accumulate a verified trade history, a trellis of attestations that grows only through real work, and peers price that history into every deal. An attacker cloning a thousand identities spends a thousand bonds but inherits no shared trust, so the attack never pays for itself.
